title: Prior Art Sweep Schema
description: Schema for .claude/metadata/prior-art-sweep.json — configuration for the --prior-art sweep run by /enhancement and /proposal before an artifact body is composed. Framework-owned and hub-shared: this file is read-only in user projects, so it carries no project-settable values. The reviewSweep toggle lives in framework-config.json.

version.description: Schema revision of this data file

searchSurfaces.description: Surfaces the sweep searches. Resolved against the consuming project at sweep time — never assumed to exist. A configured surface absent from disk is skipped, not fatal. Zero surfaces resolving is a FAILED sweep (PARTIAL), not an empty one.

projectRoots.description: Candidate source roots, in priority order. Generic across project shapes because this file is read verbatim from the hub by projects with no framework layout. An entry is either a literal directory name (`src`) or a glob pattern whose FIRST path segment contains a wildcard (`*/src`, `pkg-*/docs`). Patterns exist so multi-root and monorepo layouts, whose code sits one level down, resolve a surface at all instead of PARTIAL-ing every sweep (#2555). Depth is bounded to two segments with the wildcard confined to the first: `*/src` is expanded, `*/*/src` and `src/*` are not, and an out-of-bound pattern is reported in `skipped` rather than silently ignored. Literal entries resolve exactly as they always have.

items.description: A literal directory name, or a single-level glob (wildcard in the first of exactly two segments).

companionRepos.description: Cross-repo issue-history search over charter-registered companion repositories (#2665). Carries no repository list of its own: the list is read from CHARTER.md through companion-projects.js, so this file cannot become a second registry that drifts from the charter.

source.description: Where the companion list is read from. Prose pointer, not a list.

capabilityField.description: Entity field gating inclusion — searchable, not mere registration.

command.description: Per-companion invocation; must carry --repo, since the unscoped issueHistory command can never see a companion repo.

unreachable.description: An unreachable companion is a skipped surface, never a clean no-result: zeroResolved then degrades the report to partial.

missingSurface.description: What to do when a configured surface is absent from disk

zeroResolved.description: What to do when NO configured surface resolves. Must be partial — a sweep that searched nothing is a failed sweep, not a clean one.

excludes.description: Generated or historical trees that duplicate source hits. Without these, a sweep returns roughly three hits per real feature and authors learn to skim it.

termDerivation.description: How candidate search terms are derived. Derives from the files a change would touch, not only from feature nouns — prior work frequently shares no vocabulary with the request.

targetFiles.description: Derive terms from what a change would modify. This is the axis that finds prior work sharing no vocabulary with the request.

dispositions.description: Evidence signals mapping sweep findings to one of three verdicts

bodyFormat.description: Exact strings emitted into the artifact. Fixed here rather than restated per spec so a downstream consumer can classify a marker without parsing prose. Presence alone is NOT sufficient: a marker line may record that no sweep ran, so a consumer must match the line against the completed-sweep shapes declared here (#2542).

heading.description: Literal heading a consumer tests for

foundFormat.description: Completed sweep that found prior art, summarised on the heading line. Its entries follow as a foundEntryFormat table. Added in #2542: two swept issues already used this shape and the config did not describe it, so a consumer allowlist derived from bodyFormat classified real completed sweeps as unswept.

partialFormat.description: Incomplete sweep. Distinguishable from noneFoundFormat without parsing prose, and treated by consumers as equivalent to an absent marker.

recognisedForms.description: Marker forms the DETECTOR accepts, as opposed to the forms the commands emit (#2700). Documentation for readers of this file, who would otherwise read heading as the sole accepted form — the misreading that produced #2700. Pinned against the implementation by tests/scripts/shared/lib/prior-art-marker.test.js, so it cannot drift from classifyMarker.
